newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Money dealers say not expecting Dutch rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Money dealers say not expecting Dutch rate rise.

text.p: The Dutch central bank is unlikely to raise the special advances rate in the near-term, money market dealers said on Thursday

Earlier this week ING Barings and Rabobank forecast the Nederlandsche Bank would possibly raise the special advances rate by 10 basis points in the near future because of the recent weakness of the guilder against the German mark and the fact that Germany's equivalent rate, the repo, was at 3.00 percent.
"The Dutch central bank would only create unrest if it raises the special advances rate," said one dealer.
Another dealer said the current guilder-mark rate did not demand a move by the Dutch central bank.
The guilder was trading at 112.54 per 100 marks on Thursday, a fraction weaker compared to yesterday's 112.535 fixing rate.
One dealer said the Dutch central bank was not likely to take this step as long as the guilder was not trading above 112.67 per 100 marks.
Most dealers said interest rates and market prices would probably remain stable for the weeks to come, but one said if a change occurred, it would probably be in Germany.
"There is no reason really to raise the Dutch special advances. It would be more logic to cut the German repo by 10 basis points to 2.90 percent," the dealer said.
The Dutch guilder would probably gain some strength against the mark on a rate cut in Germany.

Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said earlier today he did not believe a cut in German interest rates would solve the country's (budgetary) problems. "I'm convinced that a cut in rates would lead to a rise in long term market rates and damage confidence in the mark," he said.
Dutch call money was bid at an unchanged 3.00 percent.
Other rates were also stable. Three month deposits were bid at 3.12 percent.
